steps.text: Call your card issuer using the number on the back of your card or in your official app, not a number from the message. Tell them it may be fraud and ask about disputing the charge and replacing the card.
Contact your bank, and the payment app too if you used one, using the number on your card or in your official app. Report the payment as fraud and ask whether it can be reversed.
Contact the bank or wire service you used right away, using the number on your card or in your official app. Report the transfer as fraud and ask whether it can be stopped or reversed.

Contact the company that issued the gift card, using the support details printed on the card or on the company's official website. Report the scam and ask whether the money can be frozen. Keep the cards and receipts.
Contact the exchange, wallet app, or crypto ATM operator you used, through its official app or support page. Report the transaction as fraud and ask about a reversal.
Uninstall any remote-access program the caller had you install, update your device's security software, and run a scan. Delete anything it flags. If you're unsure, ask someone you trust to help.

On the real site or official app (type the address yourself, don't use a link from the message), change the password for any account whose password or code you shared, and for any other account that used the same one. Turn on two-factor authentication.
Contact your bank using the number on your card or in your official app, not a number from the message. Tell them what happened and ask them to watch for suspicious activity on your accounts.
Close the page and don't enter or download anything else. If you need to reach a company, use a website you trust or a phone number you look up yourself, not the link or number in the message.
Stop sending money or information. Don't give in to pressure from the sender, and talk to someone you trust before doing anything else.
Keep evidence: screenshots, usernames, payment confirmations, receipts, and any gift cards. Don't delete messages.
Look into placing a fraud alert or a credit freeze with the credit bureaus, and watch your accounts for anything you don't recognize.
Report what happened to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Reports help investigators spot patterns.
If you lost money online, you can also file a report with the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).
